thread.title: Apple's New Low-End iPad For Students Looks To Thwart Google, Microsoft

author: BRIAN DEAGON
title: Apple's New Low-End iPad For Students Looks To Thwart Google, Microsoft
text:
Apple ( AAPL ) introduced a new lower-priced iPad at a Chicago high school Tuesday, as the company seeks to regain ground lost to Google-owner Alphabet ( GOOGL ) and Microsoft ( MSFT ) in the education market.
X The new 9.7-inch Retina display iPad supports the Apple Pencil stylus. It has a starting price of $329 for the 32-gigabyte Wi-Fi model, discounted to $299 for schools. A higher-end version, with cellular connectivity, cost $459. It sports the company's A10 Fusion chip, which first appeared in the iPhone 7.
The new device weighs 1 pound and has a 10-hour battery life and 8-megapixel camera. Previously, only the more expensive iPad Pro models could take advantage of the Pencil stylus.
Apple Plays Catch-Up Google and Microsoft have had success in recent years selling inexpensive laptops and tablets to the education market. Apple shares tumbled 2.6% to close at 168.34 on the stock market today . Alphabet shares lost 4.5% to 1,006.94. Microsoft sank 4.6% to 89.47.

Please contact customer service CLOSE The company held the product-introduction event at Lane Tech College Prep High School in Chicago. It is the company's first education-focused product event since January 2012 when it unveiled a tool for designing e-books for the iPad.
The new iPad features an aluminum body and "ultrafast wireless that can deliver two times faster cellular data connections," Apple said with the product announcement .
The display is accompanied by a powerful chip as well as enhanced cameras and sensors, including motion tracking features. The device will support the next generation of augmented reality apps, Apple said.
